analysis: Changes are limited to local operator-guidance logic and docs. In ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift, the former currentStatus is split into liveDecision (process identity, coordinator match, online status, protocol 1, writtenAt freshness and receivedAt bounds), the strict currentStatus (adds now - receivedAt <= snapshotMaxAge) and the new displayedStatus (relaxes the receipt-age check only when hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization(now) is true, i.e. the lease is unexpired). Removal decisions still go through the strict currentStatus, and removalReady is unchanged. summary() now requires removalAuthorization == authorization and removalReady() before it advises removal; otherwise it says to keep profiles. This fails closed for the MDM-removal action and matches T-053 and TB-011, which keep the stricter removal gate and a fresh coordinator decision. DoctorRunner.swift (lines 37-38, 78-79) uses displayedProviderAuthorization for display and currentProviderAuthorization for removal advice, both from the same snapshot and timestamp. Residual risk: a stale display of an App Attest lease could mislead an operator about a revocation delivered late, but this is bounded by the lease expiry, is display-only, and the daemon snapshot must still be written within 10s by the live process. Serving authorization remains coordinator-owned, as the final handoff checks in TB-002 and TB-011 apply. The doc update in provider-authorization.md lines 92-106 matches the code. I could not review the status command or the unenroll callers of summary(), since they are not in the supplied units. Other callers of the changed summary() signature were not supplied. The unenroll path is described in the docs as rechecking readiness before and after profile inspection and was not verified here. No security regression identified.
